claim.text: Covid negative despite symptoms, being close to patient? Here's why

generated_queries.english_translation: Covid negative despite symptoms, being close to patient? Here's why

native_retrieval.title: COVID-19 Exposure, But No Symptoms
native_retrieval.snippet: * Exposure (close contact) to a person with diagnosed or suspected COVID-19. * Confirmed patients have a positive COVID-19 test. * Suspected patients are those whom a doctor suspects of having COVID-19, based on symptoms. * You or your child have no symptoms of COVID-19. * To meet the high demand for COVID-19 information, when possible, find your answers online. * Always follow the most current CDC recommendations if they are different than those in this care guide. * The most common symptoms are sore throat, headache, cough and fever. Some can have no symptoms, but still spread the disease. * **Incubation period:** average 5 days (range 2 to 14 days) after coming in contact with the secretions of a person who has COVID-19. Check the CDC website to see if you and your child are current on your vaccines. * If your child becomes sick and develops more than mild symptoms, you may need to get a COVID-19 test or see your doctor.

native_retrieval.title: COVID-19 symptoms and what to do
native_retrieval.snippet: # COVID-19 symptoms and what to do. ## Symptoms of COVID-19. For some people, it can be a more serious illness and their symptoms can last longer. Try to stay at home and avoid contact with other people if you or your child have symptoms and either:. You can go back to your normal activities when you feel better or do not have a high temperature. Most people do not need to take a COVID-19 rapid lateral flow test if they have symptoms. * try to stay at home and avoid contact with other people for 3 days after the day the test was taken if you or your child are under 18 years old – children and young people tend to be infectious for less time than adults. * try to stay at home and avoid contact with other people for 5 days after the day you took your test if you are 18 years old or over. But there are things you can do to help ease some of the symptoms, such as a high temperature, a cough and breathlessness.

native_retrieval.title: COVID-19 FAQs: If you or someone in your family is sick with COVID-19
native_retrieval.snippet: ## COVID-19. # COVID-19 FAQs: If you or someone in your family is sick with COVID-19. If you are sick with COVID-19 (confirmed) or suspect you are infected with the virus that causes COVID-19, you very likely have many questions concerning your condition and health. What should I do if I had a high-risk exposure to someone with COVID-19? If I have COVID-19, can I leave my home at all? ### Q:How long must I be in home isolation (self-quarantine) if I test positive? If you test positive for COVID-19 you should isolate for**a minimum of 5 days**from the start of symptoms AND after at least 24 hours of symptoms in the absence of fever-reducing medications and with improvement of other COVID-19 symptoms. You may discontinue home isolation when at least five days have passed since the date of your first positive COVID-19 diagnostic test and you have no subsequent illness. If you had significant contact with someone with a confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis, you should quarantine following your exposure.
